topic: Claude Fable 5 Alternatives: Best Models to Use After the Export Ban
summary: On June 12, 2026, US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick ordered Anthropic to block foreign nationals from Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 under EAR export controls. Anthropic shut both models globally within 90 minutes. Fable 5 had launched just 3 days earlier (June 9) as Anthropic's first publicly available Mythos-class model with 1M token context, 128K output, priced at $10/$50 per M tokens. As of June 19, Trump signaled softened stance; Anthropic added ID verification to privacy policy — a likely path to US-only restoration. This is the first time US export controls have taken a commercially released AI model API offline.

event.why: US Commerce Dept invoked EAR — foreign nationals blocked from Mythos-class capabilities
event.impact: All users worldwide cut off, including US citizens; only Fable 5 and Mythos 5 affected; Opus 4.8, Sonnet 4.6, Haiku 4.5 remain available
event.restorationOutlook: Trump (June 19) no longer views Anthropic as security threat; Anthropic added government-ID/biometric data collection to privacy policy — likely US-only restoration in progress. No timeline.

runbook: 1. Identify all code references to claude-fable-5 and claude-mythos-5
2. Replace with claude-opus-4-8 as immediate fallback
3. Evaluate GPT-5.5 or Gemini 3.1 Pro for capabilities exceeding Opus 4.8
4. For non-US teams: use Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, or Gemini 3.1 Pro
5. Consider open-source self-hosting (Qwen 3.6 Plus, Mistral Medium 3.5) for cost savings
6. Monitor Anthropic for US-only restoration — ID verification likely required
